decisions.reason: Although it is a niche agricultural crate and was only mentioned rather than strongly promoted, it fits the firm's established reusable crate know-how and its in-house development gives it capacity to refine the offer.

A foldable large container sits squarely in the firm's core reusable transport-packaging competence, and its sustained own-page presentation suggests enough strategic relevance to continue learning and commercialisation.

A stackable plastic crate is highly related to the firm's existing product and engineering base, so management is likely to retain it because the firm can easily interpret market feedback and improve it.
A medium-duty rackable pallet is close to the firm's pallet and logistics-packaging capabilities, making it a product the firm is well equipped to support despite only moderate website prominence.

The spill-retention pallet is somewhat more specialised and may be less central to the main line, but it still builds on plastic pallet expertise and the firm's absorptive capacity argues for continued exploitation rather than exit.

A plastic pallet with load retainers is an incremental extension of the firm's core packaging range, so a large German manufacturer with in-house engineering would usually keep it and iterate rather than withdraw it quickly.
